title: Review
description: Output of Phase 2 (architectural tier only; the standard tier replaces the reviewer fan-out with constraints.md injection). DBA, DevOps, and SecOps each write their block via per-agent shards the orchestrator merges.

secops.description: A SecOps finding can occupy three locations, and the property requirement reaches only two of them. concerns[] requires must_satisfy and vulnerabilities[] requires remediation, both refused at SubagentStop. compliance_flags[] is UNREACHED: its items subschema has no required list at all, so a VETO recorded as {verdict: VETO, concerns: [], vulnerabilities: [], compliance_flags: [{}]} validates SILENT, with no statute, no concern and no action - measured through the shipped hook, with the pre-change schemas as the non-zero control. That channel is named here rather than guarded: guarding it needs its own cost analysis against already-written compliance rows and is not this change's business. The set is quantified over LOCATIONS a blocking finding can occupy, taken from the artifact contract in agents/secops.md, so a fourth location added later is visibly missing rather than silently absent.

statute.description: # CUSTOMIZE: the regulation or policy this concern maps to for your domain (e.g. GDPR, CCPA, HIPAA, an internal data-handling policy). Free-form so it fits any jurisdiction.

remediation.description: This field KEEPS its name and changes its contract: what a correct fix must SATISFY, stated as a property carrying the observation that decides it ('the endpoint must be rate-limited low enough that credential stuffing and bulk scraping are not economical, measured by <observation: N requests from one source inside M seconds are rejected before the handler runs>'), or, where an authority outside you fixed the value, that value stated literally with its source named ('the webhook signature must be verified with the provider's HMAC-SHA256 scheme, per the provider's webhook docs'). Not a mechanism: 'wrap it with the global rate-limit middleware' names one implementation, forecloses the others, and cannot be checked without reading that middleware. A mechanism you weighed goes in rationale_not_checked. THE EMPTY STRING SATISFIES this field: the walker implements no minLength, and 17 of 229 already-written vulnerability rows carry no remediation at all (info 9, low 4, medium 4; ZERO of the 3 critical and ZERO of the 26 high), so '' is what a no-remediation row will become rather than a refusal. What you write here is copied into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which IS committed, and 'verbatim' is not quite true of that copy: it runs through the absolute-path redactor in knowledge-store.mjs, so a remediation that OPENS with a route loses that route ('/v1/public-feed must be unreachable without a server-validated bearer token' archives with its subject replaced). The invariant true under both redactor forms is that a LEADING path span does not survive, so put the route mid-sentence or the archived property loses its subject; everything else is copied as written. Because that copy is public and nothing but a leading path span is rewritten, never paste credential material into this field - and read that as a rule you honor, not a control that protects you: there is no length check, no pattern check and no redaction of credential material on this path, so a pasted secret validates clean and is archived as written.

rationale_not_checked.description: OPTIONAL, and never in any required list. The non-binding landing spot for a candidate mechanism you weighed in order to test a property's COST or falsify its necessity. No downstream role owes this field an action.

severity.description: This schema is the single source of truth for concern severity. The canonical panel vocabulary is blocker|major|nit (DBA/DevOps/Design emit these); SecOps's CVE-style critical|high|medium|low|info is accepted alongside it so a SecOps concern (e.g. severity 'low') validates cleanly. Distinct from the knowledge_drift_claims severity field.

must_satisfy.description: What a correct fix must BE TRUE OF, carrying in itself the observation whose outcome decides whether it is met - never HOW to make it true. A mechanism you weighed goes in rationale_not_checked. TWO ROLES ARE EXEMPT, recorded here because the rule is unreadable without it: QA and Dev own solution design through the TDD contract, so a QA or Dev concern that specifies a test, a matrix or a mechanism is IN BOUNDS, and this field is where it goes. (a) WHERE A MISSING PROPERTY IS REFUSED, stated over the PAIR that decides it - the STOPPING AGENT'S TYPE and the artifact - because a location alone decides nothing: three agent types are refused, dba, devops and secops, each stopping with its own review.<role>.json shard, on this field in Phase 2 concerns[] and on remediation in SecOps vulnerabilities[]. NO OTHER AGENT TYPE IS REFUSED ON ANY PHASE 2 ARTIFACT: design and art-director have no AGENT_RULES entry at all, and ba, dev, qa and librarian have entries that reach no review shard, so Design - a real Phase 2 reviewer - writes an unvalidated one. Measure that rather than trusting it: run one shard whose concerns[0] omits this field through hooks/subagent-stop.sh once per agent type, against a shard the current schema already refuses as the non-zero control. NOT on SecOps compliance_flags[], whose items subschema has no required list at all - a VETO recorded as {verdict: VETO, concerns: [], vulnerabilities: [], compliance_flags: [{}]} validates SILENT, with no statute, no concern and no action, measured through the shipped hook. NOT on any Phase 4 peer-review artifact (#38). (b) THE ENFORCEMENT RECORD IS DATED AND SCOPED BY DEPLOYMENT MODE, never by repository identity. WINDOW: measured 2026-08-21. POPULATION: one machine's ~/.claude/projects transcript corpus, 1638 files / 353,907 lines across 8 repositories. FINDING: 56 genuine blocks, every one of them in a project that dispatches BARE agent names from local .claude/agents/*.md files; ZERO across roughly 635 plugin-namespaced dispatches in six repositories, one of them an adopting project with 362 of them. ONE COUNTING RULE FOR BOTH FIGURES, pipeline agents only: that same project shows 365 when every namespaced agent is counted, and the 3-row difference is another plugin's agent, which this hook could not have refused under any repair. RE-DERIVATION, and run it rather than reading it: count messages whose message.content is a plain string beginning 'Stop hook feedback:\nPipeline artifact failed schema validation', group by project directory; then cross-tabulate against the subagent_type field of the recorded subagent-dispatch tool_use entries, selecting those entries by tool name IN ('Task','Agent'). BOTH NAMES, and this is the step that decides whether the paragraph re-derives at all: on the corpus above the host recorded 'Agent' 1623 times and 'Task' ZERO times, so a cross-tabulation keyed on 'Task' alone comes back EMPTY in every repository - output-identical to the zero-blocks finding it is supposed to test. ITS NON-ZERO CONTROL: the dispatch count must come back non-zero before any zero-block figure means anything; if it does not, your selector missed the tool rather than the corpus missing the dispatches. Then run the four-cell agent_type fixture ('secops', 'SecOps', 'pipeline:secops', 'agent-pipeline:secops') against the shipped hook. The installed plugin with namespaced names is the shipping default, so read this as a dated record and not as a warranty for your deployment. AND EVERY ENFORCEMENT CLAIM HERE DESCRIBES THE SOURCE TREE at that date: an installed plugin runs its own cached copy of these schemas and of the agent contracts until that installation is refreshed, so a claim true on the integration branch is not yet true in a session running the cache. Filed as #66; the correct outcome for #66 is that somebody fixes it, on which day this paragraph becomes false and a silence has no event that notices. (c) THE FAIL-OPEN DEGRADATIONS, five of them: the enforced half degrades to nothing when node is absent, when the plugin root is unset, when the active issue is unresolvable, when the artifact's mtime exceeds 30 minutes, and - dominantly, and this is the one that screens off the other four - when the stopping agent's type does not match an AGENT_RULES key (validate-pipeline-artifact.mjs:93 for the keys, :654-656 for the lookup and its early return). (d) THE EMPTY STRING SATISFIES. The walker implements no minLength and the requirement cannot be conditioned on severity, so '' is the cheapest value that satisfies this field. Measured 2026-08-21 over the bare-name deployments where the gate fires, which is a DIFFERENT and much larger population than the knowledge/issue-archive/ folder beside this schema: 17 of 229 already-written vulnerability rows there carry no remediation - info 9, low 4, medium 4, and ZERO of the 3 critical and ZERO of the 26 high. Counting the local archive will not reproduce that denominator and is not meant to. HOW THE 229 WAS REACHED, because a reader who gets a different number will blame the record rather than the glob: EVERY .pipeline directory in those deployments was walked, including the ones under .claude/worktrees; the top-level .pipeline directories alone give 101 rows and 16 without remediation. The empty-string residual itself is tracked in #71, which also carries the wider class of free-text reviewer fields that cross the same archived-and-committed boundary with no note of any kind on them. (e) THE ARCHIVE RESIDUAL. What you write here is copied verbatim into knowledge/issue-archive/<n>.json, which IS committed, and that copy runs through the absolute-path redactor in knowledge-store.mjs. A property that OPENS with a route is rewritten: origin/main today carries LEADING_SPAN (knowledge-store.mjs:147), which replaces the leading path span only and leaves the prose after it standing; the earlier ABSOLUTE_VALUE form replaced the WHOLE value, prose and all. The invariant true under BOTH forms, and the only one to rely on, is that a LEADING path span does not survive into the durable record - so put the route mid-sentence or the archived property loses its subject. Check which form is live rather than trusting this sentence: grep -n 'ABSOLUTE_VALUE\|LEADING_SPAN' plugins/pipeline/scripts/knowledge-store.mjs. Because that copy is verbatim and public, never paste credential material into this field - and read that as a rule you honor, not a control that protects you: there is no length check, no pattern check and no redaction of credential material on this path, so a pasted secret validates clean and is archived as written. (f) THE NEIGHBOUR LIMIT. This annotation warrants nothing beyond its own field: nothing about compliance_flags[], which stays unguarded by design; nothing about the severity enum above it; and nothing about agentBlock's BLOCK-LEVEL required list [verdict, reviewed_at, concerns, notes], which this change does not touch. Read that last clause exactly: the ITEM-level required list on this very subschema IS edited by this change - it becomes [severity, description, must_satisfy] - and the two lists are different objects at different depths. (g) THIS SUBSCHEMA IS DELIBERATELY OPEN, and no check in this repository enforces that. Neither it nor the other two subschemas this change edited (SecOps vulnerabilities[].items in review.schema.json, panelVerdict concerns[].items in peer-review.schema.json) declares additionalProperties, and that openness is what makes the added required field REVERSIBLE: an instance written under the new contract, carrying keys the old one never declared, still validates against the pre-change schemas. Closing any of the three turns a reversible addition into a one-way migration on the day these artifacts meet a conformant validator. DO NOT READ THAT AS A GUARDED INVARIANT: the shipped walker implements no additionalProperties keyword at all - it handles type, enum, required, properties, minItems, items and allOf - so planting additionalProperties:false on any of the three reddens nothing: not the self-test, not the hook, not the suite. It is a written invariant with no enforcement, recorded here because here is where the next editor of this subschema is looking.

rationale_not_checked.description: OPTIONAL, and never in any required list, in any of the three subschemas that carry it. The non-binding landing spot for a candidate mechanism you weighed in order to test a property's COST or falsify its necessity - which the guardrail rule asks you to do. No downstream role owes this field an action, and a fix that ignores it is not thereby wrong. Keeping it separate is what lets must_satisfy stay a property.

notes.description: Free-text reasoning. String preferred; an array of strings is accepted (agents emit both in practice).
